items.front: Early Vedic (Rigvedic) period dates and chief source?
items.back: c. 1500–1000 BCE; the Rigveda (oldest Veda, Vedic Sanskrit) is the main source.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Who first called the Aryans a distinct race, and when did they migrate?
items.back: Max Müller; Indo-Iranian speakers migrated c. 1500 BCE via NW passes into the Sapta-Sindhu.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Aryan-homeland theories: Central Asia / S. Russia / Arctic?
items.back: Central Asia — Max Müller; Southern Russia — Nehring, Gordon Childe; Arctic — B.G. Tilak.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Non-Indian sources naming Vedic gods, and where found?
items.back: Avesta (Iran); Mitanni inscriptions (Syria — Indra, Varuna, Mitra); Kassite inscriptions (Iraq).
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Sapta-Sindhu — meaning and its seven rivers?
items.back: 'Land of seven rivers': Indus, Saraswati + Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Rigvedic tribal hierarchy from smallest to largest, with heads?
items.back: Kula (Kulapa) → Grama (Gramini) → Visu (Vishayapati) → Jana (Rajan).
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Dasharajnya War — text, river, victor?
items.back: Battle of Ten Kings, Rigveda 7th Mandala, on the Parusni (Ravi); Sudas of the Bharatas won → Kuru polity.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Which Rigvedic assembly elected the Rajan and was headed by him?
items.back: The Samiti (broad clan assembly). The Sabha was a council of elders/noblemen.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Purushasukta — which Mandala, and what does it establish?
items.back: Rigveda 10th Mandala; names the four Varnas (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) — start of stratification.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Name Rigvedic women hymn-composers.
items.back: Apala, Lopamudra, Ghosha, Vishwavara — women enjoyed a relatively respected position.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Rigvedic economy type and chief crops?
items.back: Primarily pastoral (cattle prized); limited agriculture — barley (yava) & wheat; barter, little external trade.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Most important Rigvedic deity, and Varuna's epithet?
items.back: Indra (thunder/rain/war) most important; Varuna = Ritashya Gopa (guardian of cosmic order). Soma in 9th Mandala.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Most-mentioned Rigvedic river, the 'Naditama', and how often is the Ganga named?
items.back: Sindhu = most mentioned; Saraswati = Naditama (best of rivers, RV 2.41.16); Ganga mentioned only once. ~42 rivers named.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period

items.front: Through which pass did the Aryans enter India, and how was the Rigveda first transmitted?
items.back: North-western passes such as the Khyber Pass; the Rigveda was passed down by oral tradition before being written.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Most accepted Aryan homeland, and three other proposed homelands?
items.back: Central Asian steppes (Kazakhstan / southern Russia); others: Eastern Alps, Danube valley, Arctic.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: In which book did B. G. Tilak set out the Arctic theory?
items.back: 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas' (1903).
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Why did the Aryans become dominant?
items.back: Superior military technology (horse, chariot), effective warfare, organised society, cultural assimilation and better agriculture.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Two divisions of Vedic culture?
items.back: Early Vedic (Rigvedic, c. 1500–1000 BCE) and Later Vedic (c. 1000–600 BCE).
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Rigvedic 'dhanv', and the peak Munjavat?
items.back: 'dhanv' = desert; Munjavat = a Himalayan peak famed for Soma.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Modern identification of Drishadvati and Marudvridha?
items.back: Drishadvati — Ghaggar–Hakra system (the Chautang); Marudvridha — Maruvardvan, a Chenab tributary in Kashmir.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Besides PGW, Bhagwanpura and Ropar, what material evidence of the Rigvedic age is cited?
items.back: Bronze tools, weapons and ornaments, and horse and cattle bones.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Basic unit of Rigvedic society, and how was descent traced?
items.back: The Kula (family) was the basic unit; society was patriarchal — descent through the male line.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Chief officials who assisted the Rigvedic Rajan?
items.back: Purohita (priest) and Senani (army chief); the Gramini headed the village.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Was caste rigid in the Rigvedic age? Was slavery present?
items.back: No rigid caste — only early signs of Varna; the slavery system was prevalent.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Rigvedic diet and ornaments?
items.back: Both vegetarian and non-vegetarian; ornaments Karnshobhan (earrings), Kurir (head ornament), Jyochani (rings) and the gold Nishka.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Complete the verse 'I am a poet, my father is a ___, my mother ___' — what does it show?
items.back: '…a physician, and my mother grinds the grain' — occupations were not yet hereditary.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Who were the Dasas/Dasyus and the Panis?
items.back: Dasas and Dasyus — non-Aryan opponents of the Rigvedic tribes; Panis — traders/cattle-hoarders hostile to the Aryans.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Who were the 'Siri', and what was women's status?
items.back: Siri = women who wove cloth; women were relatively respected and joined rituals and assemblies.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Rigvedic farm terms Urvara, Langal, Karishu, Khilya — and where is farming described most?
items.back: Urvara = fertile land; Langal = plough; Karishu = manure; Khilya = pasture. Agriculture is described most in the 4th Mandala.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: How many seasons were known, how was exchange done, and what boat is described?
items.back: Five seasons; barter (mainly cattle), no coins, little external trade; a boat with a hundred oars.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Rigvedic gods by domain: Sky / Atmosphere / Earth?
items.back: Sky — Surya, Dyaus, Varuna; Atmosphere (space) — Indra, Rudra, Vayu; Earth — Agni, Soma, Prithvi.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Chief Rigvedic goddesses; were there temples?
items.back: Usha (dawn) and Aditi; there were no temples or idol worship — worship was through hymns and yajna.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)

items.front: Which Rigvedic hymn lists the rivers, and in which Mandala?
items.back: The Nadi-sukta, in the 10th Mandala.
items.source: APPSC GK — Early Vedic Period; NCERT (R. S. Sharma)
